# Run the assigned NCBI BLAST search through separately selected requests

Run the original sequence search and retain the information needed to monitor
and obtain its results. Keep the registered sequence, selected program, database,
hit-list size, scientific scope and caller constraints fixed. Choose the next
preparation, submission, status or result request using actual outcomes. A
different database search or a replacement sequence requires the responsible
parent's assignment; service transport does not make that scientific choice.

## Assigned request and actual operations

This resource uses service `ncbi_blast` in `api_service_assignment_v1`. Its
closed request is `{subject_ref, program, database, hitlist_size?}`. Program is
one of `blastn`, `blastp`, `blastx`, `tblastn`, `tblastx`; its required input
molecule must match the registered operand. An omitted hit-list size resolves
to 50 in the native command without changing the recorded original request.
The caller's configured NCBI contact and shared provider-access directory are

# Retrieve the assigned BV-BRC genome, feature or protein-family data

Run the public BV-BRC data query the parent assigned and return the source data
it requested. Preserve its collection, filters, selected fields, ordering and
page. Use the returned subjects and native values to identify what was actually
retrieved; a database's functional label does not establish the target gene's
measured activity.

The configured service is `bvbrc_data`. Its default Data API location is
`https://www.bv-brc.org/api`. A caller can explicitly configure another BV-BRC
deployment's base URL and request timeout. The query does not accept a URL,
credentials or arbitrary HTTP method. Public data was retrieved without an
authorization token during verification on 2026-10-23. That observation does not
guarantee future service availability.

## Specify the actual query

The request contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `collection` | `genome`, `genome_feature` or `protein_family_ref`. |
| `filters` | An array of field/operator/value predicates. They are combined with AND. An empty array requests the selected collection's first assigned page. |
| Filter `field` | The actual BV-BRC field name, such as `gene`, `feature_id`, `genome_id`, `accession`, `pgfam_id`, `plfam_id` or `family_id`, as appropriate to the collection. |
| Filter `operator` | `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `lt` or `in`. `in` requires a nonempty array of scalar values; the other operators require a scalar. |
| Filter `value` | A literal string, number or boolean, or an array for `in`. Values are encoded individually; text inside a value cannot add another RQL operation. |
| `fields` | Optional array of returned field names. If omitted or empty, the service's default fields are returned. Unknown or absent returned fields are not filled with invented values. |
| `sort` | Optional array of `{field, direction}` objects, where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Choose relevant stable ordering when comparing pages. |
| `limit` | Positive number of records requested on this page; default 25. This is a page-size operand, not an investigation quota. |
| `offset` | Nonnegative starting result offset; default zero. |

The original assignment keeps any omitted optional fields omitted. Defaults are
resolved only into the selected native request. The client sends one GET using
the documented RQL expressions, including `limit(count,start)`. It does not
retrieve subsequent pages automatically.

For example, locating reference records named ybhP can use collection
`genome_feature` and filter `{field: gene, operator: eq, value: ybhP}`. Such a
query can return proteins from many genomes. Retain each actual `feature_id`,
`genome_id`, organism label and replicon accession rather than treating every
row as the fixed gene under annotation.

To examine a particular genome's neighbors, use explicit genome and replicon
filters together with the selected coordinate interval. Preserve the source's
one-based inclusive `start` and `end` and separate `strand`. The client neither
converts them to target coordinates nor infers neighborhood membership,
homology, co-expression or functional association scores. For family queries,
keep PGF/PLF membership and family descriptions as the source's reported data.

## Choose an available operation

`api.bvbrc.query` takes empty arguments and retrieves the original assigned
query's one page. A successful response is already completed data retrieval.
There is no remote job identifier, queue or running state to manufacture, and
no status-poll operation for this service. Validated response metadata can
establish the requested usable handoff. The original practical endpoint and
configured controller determine closure; retrieving a page does not complete
the scientific annotation.

`api.bvbrc.result` takes empty arguments in the results episode. Its parent's
selector may contain only `offset` and `limit`; the original collection, filters,
fields and ordering remain fixed. An empty selector retains the original page.
When the selected effective page matches the original page, acquire the actual
retained response without another HTTP request. A different selected offset or
limit makes exactly one new data request. Changing the scientific query requires
an explicitly assigned request, rather than an unrecorded substitution.

## Read the actual page and preserve its limits

The JSON response is an array of native source rows. Result publication retains
the exact response bytes and request/response provenance and returns the rows
with page metadata. It creates no target assay, assessment or annotation. A
missing family, protein accession or condition field stays missing; it is not
evidence that the biological feature is absent. Zero returned rows is a
completed empty query result, not proof against a gene function.

Keep `Content-Range` verbatim. An observed response with two rows reported
`items 0-2/88287`; that end value must not be treated as an inclusive last row.
The next offset uses the requested offset plus the actual returned row count.
The total is reported only when the native header supplies it. A missing total
remains unknown. A continuation identifies another possible page; it does not
select another action or prove the query should continue.

Use observation times when comparing service facts. A monitor can report the
retained immediate response's terminal observation; there is no new remote job
to poll. Keep HTTP response time distinct from queue, execution and total
turnaround measurements. This provider does not invent those unmeasured
intervals or a duration forecast.

Failures preserve the actual response when one was received. HTTP errors retain
status, body and relevant headers such as `Retry-After`. A redirect is recorded
without following it. An incomplete body retains its partial bytes and cannot
establish a completed handoff. Requests are not retried automatically. Preserve
specific failure information and useful partial results so the responsible
episode can choose its next action.

## Distinguish public data from BV-BRC computational jobs

BV-BRC also has an authenticated computational AppService, separate from this
public Data API. The official AppService client uses
`https://p3.theseed.org/services/app_service`; BV-BRC's architecture documentation
also lists `https://www.bv-brc.org/services/app_service`. An unauthenticated
read-only request to the former returned the explicit JSON-RPC error
"Authentication required for AppService but no authentication header was
passed" during verification. The latter returned a Cloudflare HTML rejection;
that proxy response is different from an application authentication result.

AppService submission, monitoring and Workspace result operations are not
implemented or exposed by this `bvbrc_data` provider. Documentation about
`start_app` does not make it an available operation. Do not represent a public
data page as a submitted computational job or claim that authenticated BV-BRC
computations were tested.

keep PGF/PLF membership and family descriptions as the source's reported data.

`api.bvbrc.query` takes empty arguments and retrieves the original assigned
query's one page. A successful response is already completed data retrieval.
There is no remote job identifier, queue or running state to manufacture, and
no status-poll operation for this service. Validated response metadata can
establish the requested usable handoff. The original practical endpoint and
configured controller determine closure; retrieving a page does not complete
the scientific annotation.

`api.bvbrc.result` takes empty arguments in the results episode. Its parent's

fields and ordering remain fixed. An empty selector retains the original page.

retained response without another HTTP request. A different selected offset or
limit makes exactly one new data request. Changing the scientific query requires
an explicitly assigned request, rather than an unrecorded substitution.

The JSON response is an array of native source rows. Result publication retains
the exact response bytes and request/response provenance and returns the rows
with page metadata. It creates no target assay, assessment or annotation. A
missing family, protein accession or condition field stays missing; it is not

# Gene prediction with Pyrodigal

`genes.predict` runs Pyrodigal on the supplied sequence or selected interval.
Select `meta` or `single` and the genetic code explicitly. These are distinct
prediction models; the operation does not substitute one after a failed run.
The existing local execution binding enforces the caller's memory and scratch
limits. A short input can be unsuitable for single-genome model training;
preserve that failure rather than inventing candidates or changing mode.

Each candidate retains its interval, strand, partial-boundary flags,
translation, native model score and native confidence percentage. The
confidence describes the native gene prediction, not the correctness of a
functional annotation. Predictions remain candidates.

The numerical sheet keeps both the worker's zero-based, half-open coordinates
within the submitted region and their coordinates in the original sequence.
It measures candidate nucleotide length, protein length excluding stop
symbols, internal stops and terminal stops. The region's coding coverage is
the union of valid candidate intervals divided by the submitted nucleotide
length, so overlaps and repeated intervals do not multiply coverage. Missing
or invalid candidate fields remain explicit; coverage from only the valid
subset is marked incomplete. An empty successful prediction differs from a
failed prediction.

Preserve the complete native candidate list and populated numerical sheet.
Return the parent's requested candidate measurements and coordinate mappings.
Native score values and derived measurements remain separate; no function
confidence or annotation-credit formula is assigned by this tool.

# Actual practical HPC operations

These operations exist in the opt-in practical HPC binding. Their presence in
this library does not make them available in a different binding. The caller
must supply a real `pbs_ssh` configuration: `workspace`, `ssh_argv`,
`python_executable` and `account`. No transport, credentials, queue or software
is discovered or selected automatically by that configuration.

| Callable operation | Actual selected work |
| --- | --- |
| `practical.inspect` | Observe the original assignment's declared path predicates. |
| `practical.inventory.refresh` | Read a selected structured catalog within the workspace and reconcile the local mirror. |
| `practical.context.set` | Persist a validated cwd and explicit environment for later actions. |
| `practical.directory.create` | Create a selected project directory. |
| `practical.file.write` | Write the exact selected UTF-8 text in project storage. |
| `practical.file.read` | Read a selected byte window, retaining original bytes and offsets. |
| `practical.command.run` | Run one selected preparation or diagnostic command on the configured remote host, retaining its outcome and logs. |
| `practical.job.start` | Submit the fixed requested job with selected `queue` and `resources`; the caller owns the account. |
| `practical.job.status` | Observe the original PBS execution, exposed scheduler fields and log tails. |
| `practical.job.collect` | Observe that execution and validate the assignment's requested output predicates. |

`cd`/`export` within a command affects that subprocess only. Use the context
operation for persistent changes. The requested job's explicit environment is
not replaced with a preparation command's environment. The worker applies
project-confined temporary/cache defaults and records native submission state.

The original attempt is identified by a saved intent, submission token and,
when known, the actual PBS ID. Reopening reconciles that identity; an interrupted
or failed SSH/qsub reply does not establish scheduler rejection. Unknown work
is not resubmitted. An explicit `retry_failed_execution_id` may start a new
attempt only for that confirmed failed original execution. No retry is made
automatically, and retry without an actual PBS ID is unsupported.

Status/collection can receive `receipt_ref` from a scoped prior practical
handoff. They check the original job/resource identity and record the receiving
episode's observation. Native completion and declared output predicates, not a
prose claim, establish the endpoint. Existing output alone need not establish
that this job produced it; use the assignment's exact hash predicates where

# Local handles, results and failures

The original requested job has a durable disk handle and systemd execution
identity. Recovery observes that handle; it does not repeat submission because
the episode or caller restarted. Prepared, starting, running, terminal and
unknown states have different meanings. Process liveness does not establish
productive computation. A missing terminal receipt is not a successful exit.

`practical.job.status` and `practical.job.collect` expose the native outcome,
available stdout/stderr tails, original offsets and file sizes. Use
`practical.file.read` when a further log/output window is needed. Elapsed
`systemd_service_wall_seconds` includes the native service lifecycle; it is
not a separately measured queue wait or program-only execution interval.

A scoped `receipt_ref` lets a later practical episode observe an original
execution from another episode. The binding verifies the saved receipt's scope,
requested job digest and resource kind. The receiver validates its own output
requirements against that original execution; it does not rewrite the closed
launch's actions or credit.

The caller's endpoint is either a usable job handoff or successful requested
job outputs with the declared predicates. A handoff can be complete while the
native job continues. For an output endpoint, successful return and file
presence alone may not establish exact result identity: use declared file-hash
predicates where needed. Preparation commands cannot self-declare completion.
Validated endpoint completion makes future expected credit exactly zero while
preserving the final actual gain; the configured controller owns continuation.

Native execution, resource and filesystem failures retain their specific
outcomes. Unknown or active work is never replaced. A later explicit
`practical.job.start` can name `retry_failed_execution_id` only for the exact
confirmed failed current execution; repairing preparation does not itself
authorize a replacement. No retry, timer, polling cadence or forced cancellation
is chosen by this library. Source rows L3–L5.

The original requested job has a durable disk handle and systemd execution
identity. Recovery observes that handle; it does not repeat submission because
the episode or caller restarted. Prepared, starting, running, terminal and
unknown states have different meanings. Process liveness does not establish

# Pairwise sequence and selected-read alignment

`sequence.align` compares the supplied query and reference sequences.
`reads.align` compares each explicitly selected original read with the supplied
reference, preserving separate results and failures. Choose protein, DNA or RNA
and local or global alignment in the actual input contract. These operations

actual matrix, match/mismatch and gap parameters with the result. RNA inputs
retain their declared molecule; the native alignment normalizes U to T.

The retained output includes both gapped strings and zero-based, half-open
coordinate paths. The numerical sheet distinguishes paired residues,
identical pairs, substitutions, gap columns and residues aligned to gaps.
`paired_identity` divides identical pairs by paired positions;
`alignment_identity` divides them by all alignment columns. Paired coverage
divides paired positions by the complete corresponding operand length;
aligned coverage also includes that operand's residues opposite a gap.
The sheet preserves each denominator. Literal equality of ambiguity symbols
does not resolve the underlying residue.

An explicit local no-alignment result has zero aligned positions and unknown
identity. Invalid geometry cannot provide positional coverage. Native alignment
scores are model-dependent scores, not probabilities of function. Return only
the requested numerical components and correspondence; complete strings and
sheets remain retained for later explicitly scoped use. Parsing and calculation
belong to the same selected result action and do not create additional turns.

`sequence.inspect` measures the supplied sequence. `reads.inspect` measures
exactly the selected original reads and keeps each read's association with

measurements, not acceptance gates. Return only requested measurements;

# Selected-read mapping with minimap2

`reads.map` maps one explicitly selected original-read population against the
supplied reference sequences. It requires a configured minimap2 executable in
the current local binding. Select map-ont, map-pb, map-hifi, lr:hq, map-iclr or
sr and any exposed overrides explicitly. These presets do not classify the
input. This binding stages FASTA and uses `--frag=no`; sr is unpaired here,
and read-quality values are not used by the mapping program. Preparation and
execution retain the caller's local memory and scratch limits.

Every reported placement is retained, including secondary and overlapping
placements. The numerical sheet keeps native PAF matching bases and block
length separately from full CIGAR columns, gaps and paired positions. Minimap2
can exclude ambiguous symbols from its native block count. The `nn` ambiguity
quantity remains separate. CIGAR M supplies paired geometry, not equality;
`cs` describes differences in the native normalized alphabet, where N=N does
not establish equality of the original ambiguous symbols.

Coverage names distinguish whole-operand span, paired positions and aligned
positions. Reference skips are separate from deletions. Query coordinates on
the minus strand remain positions in the original query. MAPQ 255 is unknown;
zero remains a reported value. Native MAPQ and alignment scores do not measure
confidence in a proposed gene function, and MAPQ has limitations for multipart
indexes. The P/S/I/i categories do not establish independence or provide a SAM
supplementary flag.

Per-query interval unions avoid counting overlapping placements repeatedly.
Native completion and parsing completeness accompany counts; empty partial
output does not establish an absence. Complete PAF, numerical sheets and exact
row associations remain retained. Return requested measurements and relevant
qualifications, rather than all raw rows or full sheets in a prompt.
